title: Trump adviser Hassett calls on Powell to leave Fed board after renovation report
text:
White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett called on former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to leave the central bank’s board following an internal watchdog report that criticized management of the Fed’s $2.4 billion headquarters renovation.
“I think that it’s time for him to move on and to respect the independence of the Fed,” Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said Sunday on Fox News.
The Fed inspector general said in a Sept. 30 report that it found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing or administrative misconduct related to the renovation. However, the watchdog identified management shortcomings that contributed to the project's cost nearly doubling from its original estimate.
President Donald Trump responded by saying Powell “should be forced to resign from the Board.” Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday that the Justice Department wouldn't reopen a criminal investigation based on the inspector general's findings, although prosecutors could act if a separate audit uncovers evidence of criminal conduct.
The renewed pressure on Powell adds another political dimension to concerns about Federal Reserve independence, an issue closely watched by bond, currency and equity markets. Powell remains a Fed governor even though Kevin Warsh succeeded him as chair in May, meaning Powell continues to have a vote on monetary policy as the central bank confronts persistent inflation and rising borrowing costs.
Powell's continued presence is unusual because former Fed chairs typically leave the central bank's board after giving up the leadership role. Powell has said threats of investigations into him and the Fed contributed to his decision to remain.
The dispute comes after the Fed unanimously raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point last month. Hassett said he opposed the increase but defended the central bank's ability to make the decision independently. “As you saw, that Chairman Warsh voted with people to increase interest rates,” Hassett said. “I disagree with that decision, but we respect that he was doing that for the right reasons.”
Trump has said Warsh should make his own monetary-policy decisions, although he told Time magazine of the latest rate increase: “I probably would have voted against the board if I were him.”

statements.quote: However, the watchdog identified management shortcomings that contributed to the project's cost nearly doubling from its original estimate.
statements.one_line: The Fed inspector general said management shortcomings contributed to the headquarters renovation’s cost nearly doubling from its original estimate.
statements.speaker: Fed inspector general, as reported by TradingView

statements.quote: President Donald Trump responded by saying Powell “should be forced to resign from the Board.”
statements.one_line: Donald Trump said Jerome Powell should be forced to resign from the Fed Board.
statements.speaker: Donald Trump, as reported by TradingView

statements.quote: Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday that the Justice Department wouldn't reopen a criminal investigation based on the inspector general's findings, although prosecutors could act if a separate audit uncovers evidence of criminal conduct.
statements.one_line: Attorney General Todd Blanche said on October 2, 2026, that the Justice Department would not reopen a criminal investigation based on the inspector general’s findings, but prosecutors could act if a separate audit found evidence of criminal conduct.
statements.speaker: Attorney General Todd Blanche

statements.quote: Powell remains a Fed governor even though Kevin Warsh succeeded him as chair in May, meaning Powell continues to have a vote on monetary policy as the central bank confronts persistent inflation and rising borrowing costs.
statements.one_line: Jerome Powell remained a Fed governor with a monetary-policy vote after Kevin Warsh succeeded him as Fed chair in May 2026.
statements.speaker: TradingView

statements.quote: Powell has said threats of investigations into him and the Fed contributed to his decision to remain.
statements.one_line: Jerome Powell said threats of investigations into him and the Fed contributed to his decision to remain on the Fed board.
statements.speaker: Jerome Powell, as reported by TradingView

statements.quote: The dispute comes after the Fed unanimously raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point last month.
statements.one_line: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points in September 2026.
statements.speaker: Federal Reserve

statements.quote: Hassett said he opposed the increase but defended the central bank's ability to make the decision independently.
statements.one_line: Kevin Hassett said he opposed the Fed’s September 2026 benchmark-rate increase but defended the Fed’s ability to decide independently.
statements.speaker: Kevin Hassett, as reported by TradingView

statements.quote: “As you saw, that Chairman Warsh voted with people to increase interest rates,” Hassett said. “I disagree with that decision, but we respect that he was doing that for the right reasons.”
statements.one_line: Kevin Hassett said Kevin Warsh voted for the September 2026 rate increase and that Hassett disagreed with the decision while respecting the Fed’s independence.
statements.speaker: Kevin Hassett

statements.quote: Trump has said Warsh should make his own monetary-policy decisions, although he told Time magazine of the latest rate increase: “I probably would have voted against the board if I were him.”
statements.one_line: Donald Trump said Kevin Warsh should make his own monetary-policy decisions and told Time he probably would have voted against the Fed’s September 2026 rate increase if he were Warsh.
statements.speaker: Donald Trump, as reported by TradingView

statements.quote: “I think that it’s time for him to move on and to respect the independence of the Fed,” Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said Sunday on Fox News.
